about: Authored query pairs on Sakila for tools/sample_db_bench.py. label: 'equivalent' or 'different' under the declared keys minus 'drop' (not_null:T.c, pk:T, fk:T.c). A 'different' pair carries a witness: 'real' (the two queries already differ on the Sakila data) or a small database (missing columns are completed with legal values) that satisfies the remaining declarations and separates them. 'sibling' names the pair it negates.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: rental.inventory_id is NOT NULL and references inventory's key: every rental joins exactly one inventory row
pairs.left: SELECT r.rental_id, r.rental_date FROM rental AS r JOIN inventory AS i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
pairs.right: SELECT rental_id, rental_date FROM rental

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key a rental may name an inventory item that does not exist
pairs.left: SELECT r.rental_id, r.rental_date FROM rental AS r JOIN inventory AS i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
pairs.right: SELECT rental_id, rental_date FROM rental

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without inventory's key two items may share an id, and the join repeats the rental
pairs.left: SELECT r.rental_id, r.rental_date FROM rental AS r JOIN inventory AS i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
pairs.right: SELECT rental_id, rental_date FROM rental

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without NOT NULL on rental.inventory_id a rental may name no item, and the join drops it
pairs.left: SELECT r.rental_id, r.rental_date FROM rental AS r JOIN inventory AS i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
pairs.right: SELECT rental_id, rental_date FROM rental

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: payment.rental_id references rental's key: a payment joins one rental exactly when rental_id is not NULL
pairs.left: SELECT p.payment_id FROM payment AS p JOIN rental AS r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
pairs.right: SELECT payment_id FROM payment WHERE rental_id IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: payment.rental_id may be NULL (5 payments name no rental): such a payment joins nothing
pairs.left: SELECT p.payment_id FROM payment AS p JOIN rental AS r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
pairs.right: SELECT payment_id FROM payment

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key a payment may name a rental that does not exist
pairs.left: SELECT p.payment_id FROM payment AS p JOIN rental AS r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
pairs.right: SELECT payment_id FROM payment WHERE rental_id IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: language_id is language's key: the LEFT JOIN adds neither rows nor a filter
pairs.left: SELECT f.film_id, f.title FROM film AS f LEFT JOIN language AS l ON l.language_id = f.language_id
pairs.right: SELECT film_id, title FROM film

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without language's key two languages may share an id, and the join repeats the film
pairs.left: SELECT f.film_id, f.title FROM film AS f LEFT JOIN language AS l ON l.language_id = f.language_id
pairs.right: SELECT film_id, title FROM film

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: rental.customer_id is no key: a customer with several rentals appears several times
pairs.left: SELECT c.customer_id, c.last_name FROM customer AS c LEFT JOIN rental AS r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, last_name FROM customer

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: address.city_id and city.country_id are NOT NULL foreign keys to keys: both joins keep each address once
pairs.left: SELECT a.address_id, a.address FROM address AS a JOIN city AS c ON c.city_id = a.city_id JOIN country AS k ON k.country_id = c.country_id
pairs.right: SELECT address_id, address FROM address

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without NOT NULL on city.country_id a city may have no country, and the second join drops its addresses
pairs.left: SELECT a.address_id, a.address FROM address AS a JOIN city AS c ON c.city_id = a.city_id JOIN country AS k ON k.country_id = c.country_id
pairs.right: SELECT address_id, address FROM address

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key city.country_id a city may name a country that does not exist
pairs.left: SELECT a.address_id, a.address FROM address AS a JOIN city AS c ON c.city_id = a.city_id JOIN country AS k ON k.country_id = c.country_id
pairs.right: SELECT address_id, address FROM address

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: film_actor.film_id is NOT NULL and references film's key
pairs.left: SELECT fa.actor_id, fa.film_id FROM film_actor AS fa JOIN film AS f ON f.film_id = fa.film_id
pairs.right: SELECT actor_id, film_id FROM film_actor

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key a cast row may name a film that does not exist
pairs.left: SELECT fa.actor_id, fa.film_id FROM film_actor AS fa JOIN film AS f ON f.film_id = fa.film_id
pairs.right: SELECT actor_id, film_id FROM film_actor

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: film.language_id is NOT NULL and references language's key
pairs.left: SELECT f.film_id FROM film AS f JOIN language AS l ON l.language_id = f.language_id
pairs.right: SELECT film_id FROM film

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: film.original_language_id is a nullable foreign key (NULL in every film of the data): such a film joins no language
pairs.left: SELECT f.film_id FROM film AS f JOIN language AS l ON l.language_id = f.original_language_id
pairs.right: SELECT film_id FROM film

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: store.manager_staff_id is NOT NULL and references staff's key
pairs.left: SELECT s.store_id FROM store AS s JOIN staff AS m ON m.staff_id = s.manager_staff_id
pairs.right: SELECT store_id FROM store

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: joining actor to itself on its key returns each row once
pairs.left: SELECT a1.actor_id, a1.last_name FROM actor AS a1 JOIN actor AS a2 ON a2.actor_id = a1.actor_id
pairs.right: SELECT actor_id, last_name FROM actor

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: last_name is no key: actors sharing a last name multiply
pairs.left: SELECT a1.actor_id, a1.last_name FROM actor AS a1 JOIN actor AS a2 ON a2.last_name = a1.last_name
pairs.right: SELECT actor_id, last_name FROM actor

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: customer_id is customer's key: the rows are already distinct
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, email FROM customer
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, email FROM customer

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the key two customers may agree on every column
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, email FROM customer
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, email FROM customer

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: (film_id, category_id) is film_category's key
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT film_id, category_id FROM film_category
pairs.right: SELECT film_id, category_id FROM film_category

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: category_id alone repeats: a category holds many films
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT category_id FROM film_category
pairs.right: SELECT category_id FROM film_category

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the key a film may repeat a category
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT film_id, category_id FROM film_category
pairs.right: SELECT film_id, category_id FROM film_category

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: rental_id is rental's key and each rental joins one customer: the joined rows are distinct
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT r.rental_id, c.last_name FROM rental AS r JOIN customer AS c ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id
pairs.right: SELECT r.rental_id, c.last_name FROM rental AS r JOIN customer AS c ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without rental's key two identical rentals give two identical joined rows
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT r.rental_id, c.last_name FROM rental AS r JOIN customer AS c ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id
pairs.right: SELECT r.rental_id, c.last_name FROM rental AS r JOIN customer AS c ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: customer_id repeats once per rental
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT c.customer_id FROM customer AS c JOIN rental AS r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id
pairs.right: SELECT c.customer_id FROM customer AS c JOIN rental AS r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: rental_date is NOT NULL: COUNT(rental_date) counts every row
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(rental_date) FROM rental
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rental

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: return_date is NULL for the rentals still out
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(return_date) FROM rental
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rental

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without NOT NULL on rental_date a NULL date is not counted
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(rental_date) FROM rental
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rental

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: customer_id is customer's key: store_id adds no group
pairs.left: SELECT c.customer_id, c.last_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM customer AS c JOIN rental AS r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.last_name, c.store_id
pairs.right: SELECT c.customer_id, c.last_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM customer AS c JOIN rental AS r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.last_name

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the key two customers may share an id and differ in store_id
pairs.left: SELECT c.customer_id, c.last_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM customer AS c JOIN rental AS r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.last_name, c.store_id
pairs.right: SELECT c.customer_id, c.last_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM customer AS c JOIN rental AS r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.last_name

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: staff_id is no function of customer_id: a customer's rentals split between staff
pairs.left: SELECT r.customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM rental AS r GROUP BY r.customer_id, r.staff_id
pairs.right: SELECT r.customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM rental AS r GROUP BY r.customer_id

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a HAVING on the group key filters the same groups as a WHERE
pairs.left: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM inventory GROUP BY store_id HAVING store_id = 1
pairs.right: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM inventory WHERE store_id = 1 GROUP BY store_id

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a filter on the group key can move below the aggregation
pairs.left: SELECT * FROM (SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total FROM payment GROUP BY customer_id) WHERE customer_id = 5
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total FROM payment WHERE customer_id = 5 GROUP BY customer_id

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a filter on the aggregate cannot move below it: the sum is over the large payments only
pairs.left: SELECT * FROM (SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total FROM payment GROUP BY customer_id) WHERE total > 100
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total FROM payment WHERE amount > 100 GROUP BY customer_id

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a group with no row passing the filter is absent on the left and counted 0 on the right
pairs.left: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS n FROM film WHERE length > 100 GROUP BY rating
pairs.right: SELECT rating, COUNTIF(length > 100) AS n FROM film GROUP BY rating

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: rental_id is rental's key
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT rental_id) FROM rental
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rental

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: customer_id repeats once per rental
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM rental
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rental

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: UNION ALL keeps the repeated store ids
pairs.left: SELECT store_id FROM customer UNION ALL SELECT store_id FROM staff
pairs.right: SELECT store_id FROM customer UNION DISTINCT SELECT store_id FROM staff

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: rental_duration is NOT NULL: every film passes exactly one of the two filters
pairs.left: SELECT film_id FROM film WHERE rental_duration > 5 UNION ALL SELECT film_id FROM film WHERE rental_duration <= 5
pairs.right: SELECT film_id FROM film

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: length may be NULL: such a film passes neither filter
pairs.left: SELECT film_id FROM film WHERE length > 100 UNION ALL SELECT film_id FROM film WHERE length <= 100
pairs.right: SELECT film_id FROM film

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: customer_id is NOT NULL on both sides: INTERSECT and IN agree
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id FROM rental INTERSECT DISTINCT SELECT customer_id FROM payment
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT r.customer_id FROM rental AS r WHERE r.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM payment)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: INTERSECT matches NULLs, IN does not
pairs.left: SELECT rental_id FROM payment INTERSECT DISTINCT SELECT rental_id FROM payment WHERE staff_id = 2
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT p.rental_id FROM payment AS p WHERE p.rental_id IN (SELECT rental_id FROM payment WHERE staff_id = 2)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: inventory_id is NOT NULL on both sides: EXCEPT and NOT IN agree
pairs.left: SELECT inventory_id FROM inventory EXCEPT DISTINCT SELECT inventory_id FROM rental
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT i.inventory_id FROM inventory AS i WHERE i.inventory_id NOT IN (SELECT inventory_id FROM rental)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: payment.rental_id has NULLs: EXCEPT keeps the NULL (nothing on the right matches it), NOT IN drops it
pairs.left: SELECT rental_id FROM payment EXCEPT DISTINCT SELECT rental_id FROM rental
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT p.rental_id FROM payment AS p WHERE p.rental_id NOT IN (SELECT rental_id FROM rental)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: IN and a correlated EXISTS select the same customers
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id FROM customer WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM payment WHERE amount > 10)
pairs.right: SELECT c.customer_id FROM customer AS c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payment AS p WHERE p.customer_id = c.customer_id AND p.amount > 10)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: language_id is language's key: the subquery returns each id once
pairs.left: SELECT f.film_id FROM film AS f WHERE f.language_id IN (SELECT language_id FROM language WHERE name = 'English')
pairs.right: SELECT f.film_id FROM film AS f JOIN language AS l ON l.language_id = f.language_id WHERE l.name = 'English'

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without language's key two English rows share an id and the join repeats the film
pairs.left: SELECT f.film_id FROM film AS f WHERE f.language_id IN (SELECT language_id FROM language WHERE name = 'English')
pairs.right: SELECT f.film_id FROM film AS f JOIN language AS l ON l.language_id = f.language_id WHERE l.name = 'English'

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: rental.customer_id is no key: the join repeats a customer once per rental
pairs.left: SELECT c.customer_id FROM customer AS c WHERE c.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM rental)
pairs.right: SELECT c.customer_id FROM customer AS c JOIN rental AS r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: rental.inventory_id is NOT NULL: NOT IN never meets a NULL
pairs.left: SELECT inventory_id FROM inventory WHERE inventory_id NOT IN (SELECT inventory_id FROM rental)
pairs.right: SELECT i.inventory_id FROM inventory AS i WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rental AS r WHERE r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: payment.rental_id has NULLs among the small payments: NOT IN returns no row at all
pairs.left: SELECT rental_id FROM rental WHERE rental_id NOT IN (SELECT rental_id FROM payment WHERE amount < 2)
pairs.right: SELECT r.rental_id FROM rental AS r WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payment AS p WHERE p.amount < 2 AND p.rental_id = r.rental_id)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without NOT NULL on rental.inventory_id a NULL there makes NOT IN return nothing
pairs.left: SELECT inventory_id FROM inventory WHERE inventory_id NOT IN (SELECT inventory_id FROM rental)
pairs.right: SELECT i.inventory_id FROM inventory AS i WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rental AS r WHERE r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: customer_id is NOT NULL: the filter removes nothing
pairs.left: SELECT payment_id FROM payment WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
pairs.right: SELECT payment_id FROM payment

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: 5 payments have no rental
pairs.left: SELECT payment_id FROM payment WHERE rental_id IS NOT NULL
pairs.right: SELECT payment_id FROM payment

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: first_name is NOT NULL: COALESCE never takes its second argument
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id, COALESCE(first_name, '') AS n FROM customer
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, first_name AS n FROM customer

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: email may be NULL
pairs.left: SELECT customer_id, COALESCE(email, '') AS n FROM customer
pairs.right: SELECT customer_id, email AS n FROM customer

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: r.rental_id is NOT NULL on a matched row and NULL on a padded one: the filter keeps only matched rows
pairs.left: SELECT c.customer_id, r.rental_id FROM customer AS c LEFT JOIN rental AS r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE r.rental_id IS NOT NULL
pairs.right: SELECT c.customer_id, r.rental_id FROM customer AS c JOIN rental AS r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: the filter accepts NULL, so customers without a rental stay on the left
pairs.left: SELECT c.customer_id, r.rental_id FROM customer AS c LEFT JOIN rental AS r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE r.return_date IS NULL
pairs.right: SELECT c.customer_id, r.rental_id FROM customer AS c JOIN rental AS r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE r.return_date IS NULL

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a WHERE on the right side's column turns the LEFT JOIN into an inner join with that condition
pairs.left: SELECT f.film_id, i.inventory_id FROM film AS f LEFT JOIN inventory AS i ON i.film_id = f.film_id WHERE i.store_id = 1
pairs.right: SELECT f.film_id, i.inventory_id FROM film AS f JOIN inventory AS i ON i.film_id = f.film_id AND i.store_id = 1

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a condition in ON keeps the films with no copy in store 1 (padded), a WHERE drops them
pairs.left: SELECT f.film_id, i.inventory_id FROM film AS f LEFT JOIN inventory AS i ON i.film_id = f.film_id AND i.store_id = 1
pairs.right: SELECT f.film_id, i.inventory_id FROM film AS f LEFT JOIN inventory AS i ON i.film_id = f.film_id WHERE i.store_id = 1

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a filter on the partition column removes whole partitions: ranks inside the rest do not change
pairs.left: SELECT payment_id, customer_id, r FROM (SELECT payment_id, customer_id, amount, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY amount) AS r FROM payment) WHERE customer_id = 5
pairs.right: SELECT payment_id, customer_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY amount) AS r FROM payment WHERE customer_id = 5

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a filter on amount removes rows inside each partition and changes the ranks of the rest
pairs.left: SELECT payment_id, customer_id, r FROM (SELECT payment_id, customer_id, amount, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY amount) AS r FROM payment) WHERE amount > 5
pairs.right: SELECT payment_id, customer_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY amount) AS r FROM payment WHERE amount > 5

not_scored.label: different
not_scored.why: staff.store_id is no key: a store with no employee (or with two) does not return one row
not_scored.left: SELECT s.store_id FROM store AS s JOIN staff AS m ON m.store_id = s.store_id
not_scored.reason_not_scored: the algebraic prover answers not_equivalent (correct: the label's own witness separates the pair) but its counterexample is a store row with no staff row, which violates store.manager_staff_id's foreign key; the foreign keys of store and staff form a cycle, and every legal completion the harness tries (type defaults for the missing columns, parent rows for the foreign keys) makes the two queries agree, so the refutation cannot be replayed
